name: Kuchisake-onna
description: A malevolent female figure of Japanese urban legend who covers her mouth with a surgical mask and asks 'Am I beautiful?' before revealing a mouth slit ear-to-ear. The modern legend caused a documented school-route panic across Japan in 1979.
full_description: Kuchisake-onna ('slit-mouthed woman') is a malevolent figure of modern Japanese urban legend, classified by folklorist and manga artist Shigeru Mizuki as a yōkai and described as the onryō (vengeful spirit) of a woman whose mouth was slit from ear to ear. She typically appears at night to lone walkers — most often schoolchildren — wearing a surgical mask, hand fan or handkerchief over her face. She asks 'Watashi, kirei?' ('Am I beautiful?'); on receiving an answer she reveals her mutilated mouth and asks again. Depending on the response and the local variant, she either kills the victim with scissors, knife or other sharp implement, or cuts the victim's mouth to match her own. The legend draws on older Edo-period (17th–19th century) folk traditions, but the modern story crystallised in Gifu Prefecture in late 1978 and spread nationally through 1979 newspaper coverage, producing a school-route panic in which children walked home in adult-escorted groups.
origin: Originated in Gifu Prefecture, Japan, in late 1978 and spread nationally through Japan in 1979. Subsequent transmission carried the legend to South Korea and into the worldwide horror-media imaginary.

etymology.origin: Japanese 口裂け女 kuchi-sake-onna, literally 'mouth-slit woman'
etymology.first_use: Recorded in modern form from late 1978; subsequently catalogued as a yōkai by Shigeru Mizuki.
